name: COINCHE
description: Belote Coinchée (often simply 'La Coinche') is the strategic, bidding-focused evolution of classic Belote. Unlike the standard game where players simply accept or pass a turned card, Coinche involves a full auction where partnerships bid to reach a specific score (e.g., '100 Hearts' or '120 Spades'). The defining mechanic is 'Coincher' (to double) when you believe the opponents cannot make their contract, and 'Surcoincher' (to redouble) if you are confident they can. It is widely considered the most skillful and competitive version of Belote.

Unlike the standard game where players simply accept or pass a turned card, Coinche involves a full auction where partnerships bid to reach a specific score (e.g., '100 Hearts' or '120 Spades'). The defining mechanic is 'Coincher' (to double) when you believe the opponents cannot make their contract, and 'Surcoincher' (to redouble) if you are confident they can. It is widely considered the most skillful and competitive version of Belote.
Evolved from standard Belote in the mid-20th century to satisfy players who wanted more control than the random 'turned card' offered. The bidding system draws inspiration from Bridge.
Standard 32-card French pack (Piquet deck), score pad.
All 32 cards are dealt at once (usually in batches of 3-2-3). Bidding starts immediately after the deal.
